headline: The hypothesis this round was raised on is FALSE. No client code persists or re-requests the expired Apps Script redirect target. The one defect found is in the instrument that was going to be used to judge the round.

operator_production_capture.source: KM.transport.metrics(), reported by the operator after the S3-R4 shipping-loop fix was published

arithmetic_that_follows_from_it.physical_http_attempts: 50 logical + 22 retries = 72; record() is called once per settled logical request, so `requests` is logical
arithmetic_that_follows_from_it.recovery_success_rate: 22 recoveries were attempted and 16 requests still ended REDIRECT_TARGET_NOT_FOUND, so roughly 6 of 22 recoveries succeeded (~27%)
arithmetic_that_follows_from_it.what_that_means: The bounded single recovery is behaving exactly as designed and is not working most of the time. A fresh attempt 200-400 ms later is evidently landing in the same condition, which points at a condition that lasts longer than the retry delay rather than at a stale URL.
arithmetic_that_follows_from_it.peak_is_a_floor: peak_concurrent_requests counted only requests dispatched through km-transport's own run(). system.health, getTable, every gap read and every write leave through _kmFetchBounded_ and were never counted. 7 is a lower bound on what was actually in flight.

endpoint_authority.instrument: assets/tests/_s3r5a-redirect-probe.js and section A of assets/tests/s3-r5a-transport-redirect-authority.test.js — the REAL km-transport module, created with an injected fetch, clock and sleep. Every URL below is a URL the shipped code built.
endpoint_authority.CANONICAL_WEB_APP_URL: https://script.google.com/macros/s/<deployment>/exec — derived from KM.DB.getApiBaseUrl() on every request, never memoised
endpoint_authority.CURRENT_ENDPOINT_AUTHORITY_RULE: The canonical /exec is rebuilt from endpoint() for every attempt, first and recovery alike. classifyEndpoint refuses script.googleusercontent.com as an endpoint class (USERCONTENT_REDIRECT) before any network call. There is no endpoint cache, no last-good endpoint and no setter anywhere in the module.
endpoint_authority.TARGET_ENDPOINT_AUTHORITY_RULE: identical — the target rule is already the implemented rule, so this round changes nothing about it

proof.scenario_1: expired redirect then a good answer: 2 physical attempts, both to script.google.com, final SUCCESS
proof.scenario_2: expired redirect then another expired redirect: 2 physical attempts, both to script.google.com, final REDIRECT_TARGET_NOT_FOUND with html_source EXPIRED_USERCONTENT_REDIRECT — it stops rather than escalating
proof.scenario_3: an unanswered read: 1 physical attempt, settles REQUEST_TIMEOUT at the 60 s bound; the timeout is not auto-retryable, so the caller pays one budget and not two

three_dispatchers_all_follow_the_same_ru.km-transport run(): rebuilds from endpoint(); maxRetries 1 for reads, 0 for writes
three_dispatchers_all_follow_the_same_ru.operation-system-db-api _kmGapRead_: its own bounded 2-attempt loop, url rebuilt from `base` each attempt, and it asks the shared transport's isAutoRetryable rather than deciding for itself
three_dispatchers_all_follow_the_same_ru.operation-system-db-api getOperationDbTa: one extra attempt on REDIRECT_TARGET_NOT_FOUND only, rebuilt from OP_DB_API_BASE_URL

recovery_contract.why_not: A write is refused by the retry predicate AND capped at zero retries by the dispatcher. Either alone would stop a replay; both are present. The mutation suite has to remove both to produce one, and does, so the redundancy is asserted rather than assumed.
recovery_contract.recovery_is_replacement_not_parallel: measured: peakConcurrentRequests never exceeds 1 for a recovered request, and openRequests returns to 0

concurrency.instrument: assets/tests/_s3r5a-concurrency.js — index.html in headless Chrome with a transport stub that HOLDS each answer for 900 ms, because a stub that answers instantly reports every page as perfectly serial.
concurrency.defect_found: peakConcurrentRequests() undercounts. Requests dispatched through _kmFetchBounded_ never incremented _openRequests.
concurrency.fix: km-transport gains openExternal(), a counter-only handle that records no sample; _kmFetchBounded_ opens it and closes it in a finally. No request is shared, delayed, retried or cancelled.

rapid_navigation_walk.description: four routes with no settle window between them — fc-summary, skuDetails, sku-regional-details, shippingplan
rapid_navigation_walk.ORPHANED_REQUESTS: 2 — the SKU Details and SKU Regional workspace reads both stayed in flight after their route had been left. Nothing aborts them.
rapid_navigation_walk.SUPERSEDED_REQUESTS: fc-summary issued nothing at all in this walk; it was superseded before dispatch
rapid_navigation_walk.not_fixed_this_round: Aborting a read because its route was left is a lifecycle decision, not a transport one, and §13 reserves loading-architecture decisions for the operator. It is measured and recorded, not changed.

sequential_walk.fc_summary: 2 requests, max 2 open — slice=bootstrap and slice=regular. DIFFERENT questions, so staged hydration by design and NOT a duplicate; the include flags were read off the wire to establish that.
sequential_walk.product_strategy: 0 requests — feature-gated off in this build, refuses before the transport
sequential_walk.weekly_shipping_plan: 2 requests on entry and 2 on re-entry — system.health and the workspace read, bounded, which is the S3-R4 fix holding

health_probe.owner: KM.DB.checkDeploymentContract, reached only from KM.DB.checkPageDeploymentContract, called only from assets/js/pages/shipping-plan.js
health_probe.DUPLICATE_HEALTH_PROBES: NOT PROVEN — measured in a browser, entering Weekly Shipping Plan twice issued one probe each time, sequentially. §5 forbids optimising a deliberate health check without proving duplication, so nothing was deduplicated.
health_probe.what_14_probes_means: 14 page reads of Weekly Shipping Plan in that session, not a fan-out. One owner, one probe per read.
health_probe.if_a_later_round_proves_it: km-transport's metadata single-flight latch already names system.health and already evicts on either outcome; _kmGapRead_ simply does not route through it. That is where the deduplication would go.
health_probe.dead_surface_noted: KM.DB.getSystemHealth exists and has no caller in shipped code. It is an operator console affordance, unbounded and unclassified, and is left alone.

timeout_interaction.detail: The 60 s bound is created per attempt, which would double the wait if a timeout were retryable — it is not, and the mutation suite plants the single edit that would make it so.

correlation.rule_applied: §8 — do not claim a shared root cause unless measured. None of the four is claimed.
correlation.PSB_TIMEOUT_EXPLAINED_BY_TRANSPORT: NOT_PROVEN — and not reachable here at all: the feature is gated off in this build, so the board issues zero requests
correlation.what_the_evidence_does_support: The transport does what it claims. 66% of production requests failed, 15 of them at the 60 s bound, and the repository's own prior measurement (boot-read-arbiter.js) records a workspace read whose EXECUTION alone was 55 000 ms. A backend at or past its limit explains both families at once: a queued /exec means the single-use echo target can expire before the browser reads it, which surfaces as REDIRECT_TARGET_NOT_FOUND rather than as slowness. That is a coherent reading, not a measurement, and it is recorded as such.
correlation.what_would_settle_it: One production capture of serverDurationMs and tablesRead from the response meta of skuDetails.workspace.get and productPricing.workspace.get. Both actions already return them; nothing has to be deployed to collect them.

not_done_and_why.orphan request cancellation: measured, but cancelling a read because its route was left is a lifecycle decision the operator owns
not_done_and_why.raising the timeout: §14 forbids it as a primary fix, and the backend is not proven bounded
not_done_and_why.anything on the write path: §12 — the production case where Pricing Confirm reported 404 and the database had changed needs write identity, a receipt and commit truth before any replay is safe. WRITE_AUTOREPLAY_ADDED = NO.
